defendants: Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation, SOS Entity No. 3438768; principal address and agent Saliman Osmani at 1201 S. Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380); Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. (California corporation, SOS Entity No. B20250280641, formed Sept. 2, 2025; principal address and agent Sheran Osmani at 7156 Golden State Highway, Bakersfield, CA 93308); DOES 1-20
causes: Violation of Unfair Competition Law, B&P Code §17200 (Count 5)
key_facts: On April 4, 2023, Plaintiff purchased a 2014 Volvo VNL diesel semi-truck (VIN: 4V4NC9EH6EN142206) from Diamond for $26,900.00 (total charges $27,092.75) with >$12,000 down payment and remaining balance financed by third-party lender. At time of sale, truck suffered a severe DEF/emissions system defect affecting the selective catalytic reduction (SCR) system, rendering it non-compliant with California emissions regulations and unsafe for highway operation. The pleadings allege on information and belief that Diamond concealed and failed to disclose: (1) the emissions defect; (2) the truck's regulatory non-compliance; (3) a prior owner's written or verbal disclosure of the DEF system failure and engine derate condition before resale; and (4) a California enforcement agency out-of-service designation. The prior-owner disclosure and enforcement designation remain unconfirmed and subject to investigation and discovery. Shortly after purchase while operating under Lease-On Owner Operator Agreement, truck experienced catastrophic emissions failure, entered 'limp mode,' emitted excessive black smoke, became incapable of exceeding approximately 35 mph, rendering it commercially unusable and unsafe. Plaintiff unable to mitigate by renting/purchasing replacement vehicle due to capital exhaustion. Per the Declaration in Support of Default Judgment (Attachment 4b to the July 20, 2026 CM-110 Case Management Statement), documented out-of-pocket losses total $20,218.65: deposit (Retail Buyer's Order) $12,345.10; GAP Addendum enrollment $1,895.00; CA DMV fees $3,442.00 (billed, outstanding, penalties accruing); Brannon Tire (emergency tire/road service) $1,197.34; Mobile Will's Truck/Auto Repair Shop $740.00; Golden Empire Towing, Inc. $562.50; Western Truck Center (lamp/parts) $36.71. Additional undocumented out-of-pocket losses (sworn testimony, no receipt) total $5,750.00: Commercial Towing (CVC §22852 storage release) $750.00; Almaraz Diesel (DEF/SCR diagnostic and repair) $5,000.00. Lost commercial income for the default prove-up is conservatively calculated at $23,400.00 (18 weeks × $1,300/week) — a deliberately conservative sworn figure distinct from the broader >$46,800 projected lost-income theory pursued against both defendants at trial. Prejudgment interest under Civ. Code §3287(a) (7%, ~3.04 years) adds $4,302.55, for a compensatory subtotal of $53,671.20, plus $25,000.00 in punitive damages under Civ. Code §3294 — a default judgment prove-up total of not less than $78,671.20 plus costs of suit, sought against Diamond alone. California Secretary of State bizfile records retrieved August 28, 2026: Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. (Entity No. 3438768) is an active California general stock corporation formed February 2, 2012, in good standing with SOS/FTB/agent, principal and mailing address 1201 S. Soderquist Road, Turlock, CA 95380, individual agent for service of process Saliman Osmani at the same Turlock address. Alpine Truck Sales, Inc. (Entity No. B20250280641) is an active California general stock corporation formed September 2, 2025 — after the April 4, 2023 sale and before this action was filed February 13, 2026 — in good standing, principal and mailing address 7156 Golden State Highway, Bakersfield, CA 93308, individual agent for service of process Sheran Osmani at the same Bakersfield address. The two agents share the Osmani surname. Alpine's SOS principal/agent address is Kern County, not the Turlock lot where Alpine was served July 1, 2026.
procedural_status: Filed Feb. 13, 2026 (STK-CV-UF-2026-0001094). Diamond served / re-served; Alpine personally served July 1, 2026. Renewed default judgment packets for both were prepared as Aug. 12 CMC hand-up material seeking ≥$78,671.20 joint-and-several, but the CMC did not convert to a prove-up: Diamond and Alpine appeared through retained counsel (Gulomjon Azimov), who disputed service and the validity of the Proof of Service on the record. No default was entered. The court ordered the case at issue by the next hearing and set a further CMC for Dec. 11, 2026; parties waived notice and are to meet and confer on service in the interim. Plaintiff emailed Azimov August 31 offering (A) Notice of Acknowledgment of Receipt or (B) sheriff re-service on the SOS agents, with a September 4 reply date. Azimov replied September 1 at 10:56 p.m. asking for ten more days after short-notice international travel. Draft reply (unsent) grants through Friday, September 11, 2026 only; silence that day means path (B). The December 11 at-issue order is unchanged. This confirms the clerk's prior default-request rejections were on solid service-defect grounds. Post-judgment collection forms remain pre-drafted but are moot unless service is cured and a fresh default effort succeeds; the now-stale readiness audit is in internal/docs/MATTER_12_POST_JUDGMENT_READINESS.md. Aug. 28, 2026 SOS bizfile printouts now pin re-service: Diamond on Saliman Osmani at the Turlock Soderquist address (Stanislaus); Alpine on Sheran Osmani at 7156 Golden State Highway, Bakersfield (Kern) — do not re-serve Alpine at Turlock. The July 1 Alpine POS named Usmani at Soderquist; SOS spells the family Osmani and places Alpine's agent in Bakersfield. Kern Sheriff returned the Alpine SER-001 Aug. 31, 2026 (item 3b(2) must be blank when 3b(3) lists an agent); corrected packet re-rendered the same day; Alpine Kern service still underway. Stanislaus returned POS-010 levy 2026003531 (certified Sept. 9, 2026): Amended Summons and FAC personally delivered Sept. 8, 2026, 9:35 a.m., Deputy P. Heaney, to Musdaqem Usmani/Manager at 1201 S. Soderquist Road, Turlock, party named Diamond Truck Sales, Inc. That is the right entity and the right Diamond address, but not the designated SOS agent Saliman Osmani, and POS-010 item 6 is completed “as an individual defendant” rather than on behalf of the corporation under CCP § 416.10. CCP § 412.30 bars default against the corporation if the summons notice is missing. Same family of trap as the clerk’s July 30 “not served as sued” rejection of the Alpine Turlock proof (that one also named Usmani/Manager at Soderquist, plus the wrong entity’s lot). Do not treat Sept. 8 as the start of Diamond’s 30-day clock and do not request default on this proof. File it as diligence / CMC record. Azimov already appeared, so the default track stays closed until service is cured or he accepts (NAR/stip). Open diligence remaining: Gobbato/Altamont standing on the lost-income lease; DMV fee vs. use-tax exemption status. Dated service/mailing beats live in timeline.json.
damages: $53,671.20 (Aug 4, 2026 compensatory-only default prove-up briefing; the prove-up itself did not go forward at the Aug. 12, 2026 CMC because Diamond and Alpine appeared through counsel and disputed service — figure stands as the litigated-damages floor if the case proceeds to judgment): $20,218.65 documented out-of-pocket, $5,750.00 undocumented sworn losses, $23,400.00 conservative lost commercial income (18 wks × $1,300/wk), $4,302.55 prejudgment interest (Civ. Code §3287(a), 7%); costs waived; punitive damages omitted from this filing. Broader case-level range still extends higher if full trial-theory lost income (>$46,800) or later punitive/§425.115 notice is pursued; also includes disgorgement/restitution under UCL §17200 and postjudgment interest.
risk: Strong compensatory case: Diamond's fraud/concealment clearly pleaded; the alleged prior-owner disclosure could establish knowledge if confirmed; catastrophic defect objectively documented; damages quantifiable. Default judgment track is closed for now — defense counsel appeared at the Aug. 12, 2026 CMC and disputed service, so the matter is back to an ordinary litigated posture unless service is cured and defendants again default. Pin down what defect defense counsel is asserting in the POS-010s on file before re-attempting service or default. Punitive damages exposure remains substantial given willful conduct post-disclosure knowledge if the case reaches trial. Aug. 28, 2026 SOS records also explain a concrete service defect: Alpine's designated agent (Sheran Osmani) and principal address are in Bakersfield, Kern County, while the July 1, 2026 proof shows personal delivery at Diamond's Turlock lot. Re-service of Alpine must go to the Kern County agent, with Alpine named as sued on the Amended Summons — do not copy the new Diamond Turlock POS onto Alpine. Diamond's agent (Saliman Osmani) is at the Turlock Soderquist address. The Sept. 8 Stanislaus POS on Musdaqem Usmani/Manager with item 6 “as an individual defendant” is the CCP § 412.30 trap: it does not start a default clock, even though the lot is Diamond’s. Ask Stanislaus for an amended POS with item 6d only if the summons notice itself was actually completed on behalf of the corporation; otherwise re-serve Saliman Osmani. Do not volunteer the 412.30 defect to Azimov.
